commit.message:
Web Audio correctness fixes: leaks, silent nodes, offline scheduling, and a multi-context crash (#225)

* AnalyserNode: fix ~28KB per-instance heap leak

shared_construction() raw-news _detail, which owns the RealtimeAnalyser and its
FFT buffers, but ~AnalyserNode never deleted it. Every createAnalyser() therefore
orphaned ~28KB that outlived context and engine teardown. Delete _detail in the
destructor (~Detail cascades the delete to m_analyser).

* DelayNode / ChannelMergerNode: default channel count to 1

Their AudioNodeDescriptor set initialChannelCount to 0, so AudioNode's constructor
initialized m_channelCount to 0 and the node's input mix / output bus rendered zero
channels: DelayNode produced no output and ChannelMergerNode merged into a zero-channel
input. Set it to 1, matching GainNode and BiquadFilterNode, to restore output;
ChannelMergerNode's output channel count is still driven separately by
m_desiredNumberOfOutputChannels(numberOfInputs).

* Offline rendering: align scheduled start/stop and ramps to the exact frame

OfflineAudioContext scheduled start(t)/stop(t) and AudioParam ramps could be off by up
to a quantum. Five coupled fixes so they land on the exact frame:

  - AudioNodeScheduler: process the first offline quantum (the initial _epoch == proposed
    epoch == 0 was skipped by the >= early-out).
  - start/stop frame = round(when * sr), not truncate (1024/44100*44100 = 1023.999
    truncated to 1023).
  - start/end envelopes 64 -> 0: Web Audio sources start and stop instantly, with no
    implicit anti-pop fade.
  - a PLAYING -> STOPPING transition exactly on a quantum boundary renders 0, rather than
    an extra full-volume quantum.
  - offlineRender advances current_sample_frame by exactly one quantum, dropping the
    odd/even +index drift that lengthened every other quantum by one frame.

* AudioNodeScheduler: schedule start/stop against absolute frames

start()/stop() computed `_startWhen = _epoch + when * sr`, treating `when` as relative to
the scheduler's _epoch. _epoch is 0 for a freshly created source but becomes
currentSampleFrame once the source has been pulled, so a source that is connected (hence
pulled, _epoch > 0) and started later began at absolute (currentTime + when) instead of
the spec's absolute `when`, drifting by ~currentTime. Drop _epoch so `when` is absolute.
This is equivalent for offline rendering (where _epoch is 0 at schedule time) and fixes
the realtime "connect, then start later" drift.

* AudioContext: apply graph edits synchronously for offline contexts

connect()/disconnect() enqueue node (dis)connections into pendingNodeConnections, resolved
on the render thread during handlePreRenderTasks; disconnects are additionally two-phase
(Disconnect -> FinishDisconnect one or more quanta later, plus a fade). An OfflineAudioContext
has no render thread while control code runs, so the whole queue only lands on the first
rendered quantum: "connect(...); disconnect(...); startRendering()" renders a stale topology
(disconnected sources stay audible), and a single-quantum render can never observe a disconnect
at all. Apply connect / disconnect / connectParam / disconnectParam synchronously for offline
contexts; realtime contexts keep the async queue (render-thread concurrency + anti-click fade).

* AudioDevice_Miniaudio: reference-count the shared ma_context

The miniaudio backend keeps one process-wide ma_context (g_context) -- it hosts device
enumeration and is passed to every ma_device_init -- but ~AudioDevice_Miniaudio
unconditionally called ma_context_uninit(&g_context). A page with two AudioContexts (which
browsers allow) has two devices sharing that context: the first device destroyed tears down
the context the second is still using, and the second destructor tears it down again.
ma_context_uninit() does not zero the struct, so the second pass calls pa_context_disconnect()
on an already-freed PulseAudio context and the process aborts:

    Assertion 'pa_atomic_load(&(c)->_ref) >= 1' failed at ../src/pulse/context.c:1077

(In between it is also a use-after-free: the surviving device keeps rendering against a context
whose backend connection was already closed.)

Reference-count the shared context behind a mutex (devices may be created and destroyed on
different threads); only the last device out calls ma_context_uninit(). Devices also track
whether ma_device_init() actually succeeded, so a failed-to-open device no longer stop()s and
uninit()s a zeroed ma_device (the "Unable to stop audio device" noise) and no longer leaks a
context reference. Device-list probing keeps its value cache but only marks itself probed on
success.

@@ -53,6 +53,9 @@ class AudioNodeScheduler
     // epoch is a long count at sample rate; 136 years at 48kHz
 
     std::atomic<uint64_t> _epoch{0}; // the epoch rendered currently in the busses
+    bool _firstUpdateDone = false;    // the first offline quantum has _epoch == proposed == 0, which the
+                                      // >= early-out below would skip, dropping the first quantum for a
+                                      // start(0) source; force the first update through (see update()).
     uint64_t _epochLength = 0;        // number of frames in current epoch
 
     // start and stop epoch (absolute, not relative)
